items.title: Food redistribution: a critical review of an overlooked priority measure against food waste
items.title_en: Food redistribution: a critical review of an overlooked priority measure against food waste
items.title_zh: 食品再分配：对一项被忽视的、旨在减少食物浪费的优先措施的批判性回顾
items.summary_en: Food redistribution is widely recognized as a preferred strategy for reducing food loss and waste. Yet it is still treated mainly as charitable relief, while its broader role in governance and the conditions for effective implementation remain insufficiently articulated. Drawing on a triple bottom line perspective and sustainable development goal coupling framework, this study synthesizes evidence from the literature, international practice, and field research in China to examine the contributions of food redistribution, the constraints that shape its performance, and the models through which it can be scaled. We find that existing research provides much stronger evidence on social benefits than on economic mechanisms or environmental outcomes, which remain constrained by value-cost mismatches, uncertainty in substitution assumptions, and limited activity data. Cross-dimensional evaluation and analysis of synergies also remain weak. In practice, international experience points to a transferable operational architecture based on hub-and-spoke networks and standardized procedures, but successful scaling depends on aligning policy tools with operational mechanisms to reduce systemic frictions. The Chinese cases extend this understanding by identifying two complementary implementation models, centralized and decentralized, each adapted to different institutional and market conditions. Together, these findings highlight the important role of food redistribution in sustainable food and waste governance, and offer practical support for integrated evaluation and wider implementation.
items.summary_zh: 食品再分配被广泛视为减少食品损失和浪费的首选策略。然而，它仍主要被视为慈善救济，而其在治理中的更广泛作用以及有效实施的条件尚未得到充分阐述。 本研究基于“三重底线”视角和可持续发展目标耦合框架，综合分析了文献、国际实践及中国实地研究的证据，以考察食品再分配的贡献、影响其绩效的制约因素，以及可实现规模化推广的模式。 我们发现，现有研究在社会效益方面的证据远比经济机制或环境成果方面的证据更为充分，而后者仍受制于价值与成本的不匹配、替代假设的不确定性以及活动数据的匮乏。 跨维度的评估以及对协同效应的分析也仍显薄弱。在实践中，国际经验表明，基于“枢纽-辐条”网络和标准化流程的运营架构具有可移植性，但成功的规模化实施取决于将政策工具与运营机制相协调，以减少系统性摩擦。 中国的案例通过识别两种互补的实施模式——集中式和分散式（分别适应不同的制度和市场条件）——拓展了这一认识。这些发现共同突显了食物再分配在可持续食品和废弃物治理中的重要作用，并为综合评估和更广泛的实施提供了实践支持。

items.title: Scientists confirm global warming is accelerating faster than ever recorded
items.title_en: Scientists confirm global warming is accelerating faster than ever recorded
items.title_zh: 科学家证实，全球变暖的速度正以有史以来最快的速度加快
items.summary_en: Earth is warming faster than ever recorded, with scientists detecting a major acceleration in global temperatures since around 2015. A new study reveals that the warming rate has surged to approximately 0.35°C per decade, nearly double the average pace observed from 1970 to 2015. After removing natural climate fluctuations, researchers confirmed the acceleration with more than 98% statistical confidence.
items.summary_zh: 地球变暖的速度已达到有记录以来的最快水平，科学家们发现，自2015年左右以来，全球气温上升速度显著加快。 一项新研究显示，变暖速率已飙升至每十年约0.35°C，几乎是1970年至2015年间观测到的平均速度的两倍。在剔除自然气候波动因素后，研究人员以超过98%的统计置信度证实了这一加速趋势。

items.title: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?
items.title_en: The asteroid killed the dinosaurs. Why did crocodiles survive?
items.title_zh: 小行星导致了恐龙的灭绝。鳄鱼为什么能幸存下来？
items.summary_en: Scientists may have solved a 66-million-year-old mystery: how crocodiles survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs. A sweeping analysis of fossils and ancient climates suggests that their preference for warm environments placed them in tropical refuges that remained habitable even after the catastrophic impact.
items.summary_zh: 科学家们可能解开了6600万年前的一个谜团：鳄鱼是如何在小行星撞击导致恐龙灭绝后幸存下来的。对化石和古气候的全面分析表明，由于鳄鱼偏好温暖的环境，它们栖息在热带避难所中，这些地区即使在灾难性撞击发生后，仍然适宜生存。

items.title: 128,000-year-old ice in Tibet could rewrite climate history
items.title_en: 128,000-year-old ice in Tibet could rewrite climate history
items.title_zh: 西藏12.8万年前的冰层或将改写气候史
items.summary_en: Ancient ice discovered high in Tibet may be more than 128,000 years old, preserving an extraordinary record of Earth's climate that scientists previously thought had been lost. The discovery reveals a rare glimpse into the last ice age and could reshape our understanding of how glaciers survive dramatic changes in global climate.
items.summary_zh: 在西藏高海拔地区发现的远古冰层可能已有12.8万多年的历史，其中保存着地球气候的非凡记录，而科学家此前曾认为这些记录早已失传。这一发现让我们得以一窥上一次冰河时代的罕见景象，并可能重塑我们对冰川如何在全球气候剧变中存续的理解。

items.title: Scientists discover a hidden oxygen reservoir deep inside Earth
items.title_en: Scientists discover a hidden oxygen reservoir deep inside Earth
items.title_zh: 科学家在地球深处发现了一个隐藏的氧气储库
items.summary_en: Scientists have discovered that magma deep inside Earth can store surprising amounts of extra oxygen, potentially revealing a hidden contributor to our planet's oxygen-rich atmosphere. The findings suggest that ancient volcanic eruptions may have helped transform Earth's atmosphere billions of years ago, with implications for understanding life on other planets.
items.summary_zh: 科学家发现，地球深处的岩浆中可以储存惊人的额外氧气，这可能揭示了地球富氧大气中一个隐藏的来源。这一发现表明，数十亿年前的古代火山喷发可能曾帮助重塑了地球的大气层，这对理解其他行星上的生命具有重要意义。

items.title: Antarctica’s “Doomsday Glacier” could raise sea levels twice as much as predicted
items.title_en: Antarctica’s “Doomsday Glacier” could raise sea levels twice as much as predicted
items.title_zh: 南极洲的“末日冰川”可能导致海平面上升幅度达到此前预测值的两倍
items.summary_en: Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier may be melting twice as much as previously predicted, even without additional global warming. Scientists discovered that warm ocean water is penetrating miles beneath the ice, weakening its foundations and accelerating its retreat. A new model predicts that the glacier could add up to 30 millimeters to global sea levels by 2100, with a 60% chance of losing a crucial stabilizing ridge.
items.summary_zh: 南极洲的斯威茨冰川的融化速度可能达到此前预测值的两倍，即使全球变暖不再加剧也是如此。科学家发现，温暖的海水正渗透到冰层下方数英里深处，削弱了冰川的基础，并加速了其后退。 一项新模型预测，到2100年，该冰川可能导致全球海平面上升多达30毫米，且有60%的概率会失去一条至关重要的稳定山脊。
